proposed.sourceName: Darul Ifta Birmingham — 'Skin Care Products Containing Glycerine or Alcohol' (Mufti Mohammed Tosir Miah)
proposed.paraphrase: A Hanafi fatwa holding plant/synthetic glycerine permissible without verification, and that where the source of glycerine is uncertain and cannot reasonably be confirmed it is permissible to assume it is halal — invoking the principle that investigating every ingredient's source causes undue hardship (answer given regarding externally-used products).

proposed.sourceName: Darul Iftaa Mahmudiyyah (Lusaka, Zambia) — Fatwa #326 on Glycerine
proposed.paraphrase: By contrast, this fatwa rules glycerine from an animal source not permissible (fat generally from a non-halal animal) and advises checking the source before use — representing the cautious side of a genuine scholarly disagreement over unverified-source glycerine.

researcherNote: E422 seeded general = grade 3 (Questionable — contested). Glycerol is frequently plant/synthetic (so not 'widely avoided'), yet animal-fat sources exist and authorities genuinely split: permissive (Birmingham: assume halal under hardship) vs cautious (Zambia: animal source not permissible, verify). Cited both sides honestly. Two independent tier-1 Sunni sources. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01.
